structure.title: Act I · The claim · Who wants a war?
structure.text: Before Henry asks whether he may lawfully invade France, two churchmen discuss a bill threatening church property. A long explanation of inheritance follows. The audience has already heard why its expert witnesses might welcome an expensive enterprise abroad.

structure.title: Acts II–III · Harfleur · What a king can ask of men
structure.text: The expedition needs recruits, supplies and disciplined obedience. Henry can stir soldiers to great efforts and can describe in terrible detail what those soldiers might do to a besieged town. Both speeches belong to his military accomplishment.

structure.title: Act IV · Agincourt · A voice around the campfire
structure.text: Disguised before the battle, Henry listens to ordinary men ask whose soul bears the cost if the king's cause is bad. The next day he must speak in his own person to men who have every reason to fear the odds.

structure.title: Act V · The settlement · Words across a border
structure.text: The fighting gives way to negotiations and to a courtship in two languages. Terms for the future of two countries enter a room where a young woman is being asked to become a wife.

people.name: Henry
people.role: King once known as Prince Hal
people.text: His former companions remember the tavern. His current colleagues require a commander. He moves between registers with extraordinary ease, while men who still count on the old familiarity find the king harder to approach.

people.name: Fluellen and Williams
people.role: An officer and a common soldier
people.text: Fluellen cares about the rules of warfare. Williams wants to know what obligation runs back from commander to the soldier who risks his life. Their encounters with Henry put different kinds of loyalty within speaking distance.

people.name: Katherine
people.text: In an English lesson she tries out words for parts of the body. Later conversation crosses the same linguistic divide with a marriage and a kingdom at stake. Her language teacher is one of her few allies in the room.

context.title: A claim through the female line
context.text: The English claim requires an argument about whether women transmit a right to the French crown. You can follow the pressure in the scene without tracing every ancestor. Henry wants an assurance somebody else will answer for before God.

notice.text: Listen for pronouns in the battle speeches.
notice.why: Calling soldiers brothers can make a frightening death bearable. There are also moments when the king insists upon the distance between his office and any man he calls brother.

notice.text: How does a threat become somebody else's responsibility?
notice.why: In front of Harfleur Henry describes violence his forces could inflict, then tells the town how to prevent it. The sequence matters for deciding what sort of victory his words achieve.

opening: Henry needs his army to believe an invasion is worth dying for. He can make the argument magnificently, turning exhaustion and terrible odds into an invitation to belong to history. Shakespeare also takes him among soldiers who have less freedom to choose what this war means. The play allows the exhilaration of leadership its full force while leaving room for the threats, evasions, and bodies behind it. A king's ability to inspire becomes inseparable from his ability to decide whose suffering a victory will require.
